To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the clinical management of PHP patients requires an accurate follow-up, (2) the clinical management requires the identification of the genetic/epigenetic alteration, (3) the genetic/epimolecular diagnosis requires a systematic clinical evaluation, and (4) the clinical evaluation is improved by a standardized healthcare pathway.
the clinical management of patients with Gsα protein dysfunction is still challenging and that a common healthcare pathway could improve their care.
the clinical management of patients with AHO/PHP is improved by the adoption of a standardized healthcare pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective and standardized clinical management for AHO/PHP subjects.
a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms and clinical consequences of GNAS alterations and their management, in order to improve the clinical care of these patients.
the identification of a standard clinical approach for the diagnosis and follow-up of patients affected by Gsα protein dysfunction, which could be useful for other European countries as well.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the clinical management of patients with AHO/PHP should be performed in dedicated centres, with a multidisciplinary team, including geneticists and endocrinologists.
the clinical approach of these patients is still not standardized and a dedicated healthcare pathway would be helpful.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
“the GNAS locus is a complex genetic locus and the clinical features of AHO/PHP are not only related to the type of alteration but also depend on the specific gene and locus alterations”.
the genetic/epigenetic alterations in GNAS locus and the clinical consequences are not as different as they were previously thought.
the clinical-molecular correlation in AHO/PHP subjects is not straightforward and that the current clinical classification is not exhaustive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clinical approach to patients with GNAS alterations should not be based on the molecular diagnosis but on the clinical phenotype.

a multidisciplinary approach, including endocrinologists, pediatricians, geneticists, radiologists, orthopedists, ophthalmologists, dentists, is needed for the management of patients with PHP and AHO.
a common healthcare pathway should be adopted for all patients affected by AHO/PHP.
